audit.whatIsWrong: Frenzied Maul is described eleven times as a 'bite that heals' or 'bite-heal sustain', and both layers are built on anti-heal, but the condition on the heal is never stated.
audit.why: Frenzied Maul only heals on the SECOND cast against the same target, and only while that target still carries the mark the first cast applied. It is also a 5-second cooldown — the shortest thing in this lane by a distance, which is why 'wait for his W' is not a plan. Together those two facts change the answer completely: you do not out-sustain the heal or wait it out, you deny it by breaking the mark, which for a champion with three dashes means stepping out for the beat between bites. The entry currently frames his sustain as a constant Ambessa has to buy items against.
audit.corrected: Frenzied Maul (W), 5s, 325 range: marks you, applies on-hit, and only the SECOND cast on that mark heals him. Break the mark between bites and the heal never lands.
sources: champ-data/_kits/volibear.json — W Frenzied Maul: 'damages an enemy, applying on-hit effects and marking them. Casting this ability again on the same target deals bonus damage and Heals Volibear', cd 5

audit.whatIsWrong: Thundering Smash is described as an 'empowered Q run' and an 'empowered-Q stun approach' that you dodge by not letting him reach you, with no cooldown given.
audit.why: The stun is not on the cast and not on the run — it lands on the first enemy he ATTACKS while the ability is active. That makes it an auto-attack you sidestep or interrupt, not a dash you dodge, and it means his approach can be entirely wasted if the attack misses its window. It is 12s at rank 1. Framing it as an approach tells a player to retreat, when the correct answer is often to hold ground out of attack range and let the timer expire.
audit.corrected: Thundering Smash (Q), 12/11.5/11/10.5/10, 300 range: he speeds toward you and the stun rides the first ATTACK he lands. Break that attack, not the run.
sources: champ-data/_kits/volibear.json — Q Thundering Smash: 'Volibear gains speed towards enemies, Stunning and damaging the first one he Attacks', cd 12/11.5/11/10.5/10

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings credit Ambessa with 'your armor-pen burst plus R's healing-on-ability-damage', 'your armor-pen burst and R-healing', 'your armor-pen burst'. Two more call Stormbringer a shield: 'his R-shield tower-dive', 'shields him into a brawl'.
audit.why: Public Execution grants no armour penetration and no healing in Riot's text — blink to the farthest champion in a chosen line, suppress, slam for damage and a stun. The kit file's 'heal' flag on R is a tooltip-parsing misfire (see notes). And Stormbringer grants BONUS HEALTH, not a shield, plus a tower disable on landing. The difference is not cosmetic: a shield decays and can be burst through before it matters, bonus health does not, so a player planning to 'burst the shield off' during his dive is planning against the wrong resource. Sky Splitter is the ability in his kit that actually shields, and only when he stands inside his own blast.
audit.corrected: Stormbringer (R), 160/135/110: leap, slow, damage, BONUS HEALTH, and it disables your tower on landing. Sky Splitter (E), 16s flat, is the shield — and only if he is inside the blast.
sources: champ-data/_kits/volibear.json — R Stormbringer 'gaining bonus Health', E Sky Splitter 'granting Volibear a Shield if he's inside the blast radius', cd 16

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns gives no number for anything — 'His engage. Dash it. Your committal tool: never spend it on chip.'
audit.why: Volibear's three relevant timers are unusually far apart and the spread is the whole shape of the lane: Frenzied Maul at 5 seconds is effectively always up, Thundering Smash at 12s is the one real punish window, and Sky Splitter is a flat 16s at every rank. A player told only to 'track Thundering Smash' will wait for a W window that never comes and skip the Q window that does.
audit.corrected: Frenzied Maul 5s, Thundering Smash 12s at rank 1, Sky Splitter 16s flat, Stormbringer 160s at rank 1. The 12s after a spent Thundering Smash is the window.
sources: champ-data/_kits/volibear.json — W cd 5, Q cd 12/11.5/11/10.5/10, E cd 16, R cd 160/135/110

I did not flip it — chart edits are atomic, mirrored against the Volibear page, and a guessed power shift is worse than a visible contradiction — but the prose is the half that matches the kit.

edits.before: Through 4-5 it's even-to-his — your cooldowns are longest here and his Maul-heal brawl is sticky, so farm and set up rather than forcing. At 6 you take over: Public Execution blinks you behind him, suppresses, and your passive armor-pen burst plus R's healing-on-ability-damage eats straight through his bite sustain, which flips this from a coinflip brawl into a kill. Don't let him reach you for the stun; bait it, dash clear with your passive, then commit.

notes: LEVEL CHART CONTRADICTS ITS OWN PROSE at three stages, left untouched — see audit point 3. This is now the third entry in my slice with the same fault (vayne, vladimir, volibear), so it is almost certainly a generator bug rather than authored judgement; a scripted comparison across all 71 Ambessa matchups would be cheaper than hand-catching them. KIT-FILE FLAG MISFIRE: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json tags Public Execution (R) with 'heal' and tags W and R with 'grounding'; Riot's descriptions support none of them (the parser caught 'slams the ground'). The invented 'R armor-pen / on-ability healing' text derived from it now shows up in urgot, vayne, vladimir and volibear — worth a file-wide sweep. WIN RATE: MC_WR_TABLES.ambessa.volibear is 47.55 while the packet reports 54.34 over 219 games. No win-rate edit proposed. UNVERIFIED, NOT ASSERTED: whether Repudiation's brace can absorb the Thundering Smash stun itself rather than only its damage — the kit files settle neither CC absorption nor cast-time priority, so I only claimed the damage half.
